items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: when I was with Woody Herman’s band when I first went with him I wasn’t a great reader but I could read adequately.

ctx.x: Walter Beeler called me into the office one day. He said, “You’ve been here for six months and you haven’t showed up to one ensemble. What is your problem?” And I said, “I can’t read music.” And he almost hit the ceiling. He said, “What do you mean you can’t read music? How’d you get into this school?” I said, “I don’t know.” So I played for him and he laughed. It was like, “You can play but you can’t read?” Anyway, that was it. Somehow I had a mental block against reading. I was afraid to do it. I was almost…
You went on to Berklee, right?
Right. Now, when was he in your band? He was in it just a short time, wasn't he?
